original_test_intent: Read the ClearLog ActionInfo metadata for one validated Manager LogService so the destructive action can be understood without deleting logs.
original_method: Resolve the selected LogService and its documented or advertised ClearLog ActionInfo URI, issue one trusted metadata GET, validate action target, method, payload and scope fields, and preserve logs.
manual_activity: Supply and approve the target firmware's real ClearLog ActionInfo URI/schema, selected LogService and expected action-scope fields; the placeholder ellipsis and Log1 assumption are not executable inputs.
required_inputs: Advertised or vendor-pinned ClearLog ActionInfo URI
ActionInfo schema and association with the exact ClearLog target
Supported method, payload and deletion scope fields
safety_requirements: Do not clear logs before inspection
agent_execution_scope: Bind BMC, Manager, LogService and firmware identity
Discover or validate canonical ActionInfo URI
Capture HTTP metadata and restricted raw hash
Validate associated ClearLog target, method, payload and scope description
Confirm no action task or entry change occurred
engineer_actions: Resolve discrepancies with the destructive ClearLog row

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its GET intent is appropriate for metadata, but the literal ellipsis is non-executable and fixed/path assumptions, `-k`, credentials and readability-only checks cannot establish ClearLog semantics.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After approving the real ActionInfo URI/schema, perform one trusted GET, validate its association and full action contract, and stop without invoking or clearing anything.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Manager/LogService ClearLog metadata GET and 15/10 timing remain; no service, URI suffix, payload or scope is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Discover ActionInfo through firmware-advertised metadata or a pinned vendor schema, then cross-check every destructive-action field against the selected service.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Removes automatic clearing, Log1 and ellipsis assumptions and adds identity, schema, secure access and a no-action proof.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Covers the declared ClearLog contract only; it neither deletes entries nor proves the action's runtime behavior.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Vendor metadata can be incomplete or inconsistent with implementation, so it is a prerequisite for—not evidence of—a successful ClearLog test.

project_override_considerations: If the firmware exposes no ActionInfo resource, a reviewed vendor schema package may satisfy metadata planning, but the agent must record that no live ActionInfo GET was possible and must not probe guessed paths.
expected_evidence: ActionInfo URI authority and schema revision
HTTP status/content type/timing and restricted raw hash
Metadata identity and associated ClearLog canonical target
Declared HTTP method, payload and affected-scope fields
Proof no ClearLog task, entry deletion, truncation or unrelated mutation occurred

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title and Procedure consistently describe a GET of ClearLog metadata. Fixed Log1, an incomplete DeepSeek ellipsis and unsafe setup are deficiencies, not competing Master test semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The vendor URI/schema, selected service and secure access package are identifiable prerequisites, so the metadata case remains REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Turns a guessed/incomplete action path into an authoritative metadata validation and structurally prevents destructive ClearLog execution.
independent_technical_reasoning: ActionInfo is safety-critical because it supplies the contract for the destructive case immediately before it. A guessed URI ending in an ellipsis is not a runnable test, and a successful response at some action-related path does not prove association with the chosen LogService. The review therefore requires a canonical metadata URI, resource identity, exact action target, supported method and payload/scope fields. At the same time, this row must be technically incapable of POSTing or clearing entries; no-action evidence is part of acceptance.
